evidence: Page 32 (§1.1.5, KV cache as a concept): "At 9.2K input tokens the canonical FP16 KV per request is ~24.1 GB on the input-only basis — 9,200 × 2,621,440 B = 24,117,248,000 B ≈ 24.12 GB — and the 8-bit raw byte-halving variant is ~12.06 GB on that same input-only basis — 9,200 × 1,310,720 B = 12,058,624,000 B ≈ 12.06 GB — against ~12.45 GB for the same 8-bit variant on the input-plus-output resident basis at 9.5K tokens, the basis Ch. 7 §3 uses for slot counting (9,500 × 1,310,720 B = 12,451,840,000 B ≈ 12.45 GB; the FP16 figure on that resident basis is ~24.9 GB, written 24.90368 GB there)."
issue: The sentence compares the 8-bit per-request figure on the input-only basis (12.06 GB) against the 8-bit figure on the resident basis (12.45 GB) and the FP16 resident figure (~24.9 GB), but omits the FP16 input-only figure in the same comparison set, leaving the reader with a partially unpaired set of figures at exactly the point where the book is establishing its two named bases. More importantly, the cross-reference "Ch. 7 §3 uses for slot counting" resolves to a subsection that is titled §7.3 "Worked Example" (page 162–169, heading "7.3. Worked Example"), not to the subsection that actually derives the slot count. The slot-counting rule ("the canonical concurrency ceiling is that resident-basis quotient floored to a whole slot — 17, not 18") and the concurrency ceiling itself are stated in Ch. 4 §4.6 (page 120: "~17 full-context requests once the ~64 GB runtime is reserved: 436 GB ÷ 24.9 GB ≈ 17.5, floored to 17"), in Ch. 7 §3 (page 168: "17.51; conservative integer floor 17") and in Ch. 7 Fig 7.7 ("The concurrency budget", listed in the List of Figures at page 9 as being on page 168). The book's own cross-reference convention (Preface, page 23) states that "§ N.M (the thin space after § is optional, so §7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference), which means Chapter N, Section M". So "Ch. 7 §3" is a legal form pointing at §7.3, but the citation is ambiguous about which figure it supports: the same paragraph also asserts "written 24.90368 GB there", which appears in Ch. 7 §3 (Table 7-1: "9,500 × 2,621,440 B = 24,903,680,000 B ≈ 24.90 GB"), so the reference does resolve. The residual defect is the missing FP16 input-only figure in the comparison set and the lack of a named slot-count rule at the point of citation — a reader arriving at the eight-bit figure cannot see the FP16/8-bit pairing on a single basis.
fix_instruction: Complete the comparison set in the Ch. 1 §1.1.5 paragraph by stating the FP16 input-only figure alongside the 8-bit input-only figure on the same basis (i.e. ~24.12 GB FP16 vs ~12.06 GB at 8-bit, input-only; ~24.90 GB FP16 vs ~12.45 GB at 8-bit, resident), and name the slot-count rule explicitly at the point of citation (e.g. "the whole-slot floor of 17 that Ch. 7 §3 and Ch. 17 apply") so the reader is pointed at the rule, not only at the number's location.
